players.note: The Week 6 game was likely an anomaly. I'm not convinced Blake Corum will have a sizable role in the future.
We're back to a committee. Warren had a nice run, but Rico is back, and Rico is Mike McCarthy's guy. This backfield will be impossibly to get right the rest of the year.

Much more explosive than Chris Rodriguez, expanding his role as a receiver...I'm betting Tuten gets back to his workhorse role on the ground after the bye week. (Also going to be slightly cheaper headed into his bye.)
The injury concerns are legitimate, but his value has dropped too far to sell. Let's not forget this was the third overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
Jacobs is returning for Week 7, and as inefficient as he's been on the ground in recent years, he's light-years better than MarShawn Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson. Must-start going forward.
Was Skattebo just getting disciplined in Week 6 for his fumble in Week 5, or is this a permanent thing moving forward? Either way, don't sell after a week where he got zero touches.

The volume is there, but Pollard is so dusty at this point and this run game is not competent enough to ever feel great about starting Pollard. I'd try to sell for a younger asset who maybe hasn't broken out yet, but has a chance to expand their role.

Back-to-back double-digit fantasy performances from Corum likely have some people excited about his rest-of-season projections. I'm still of the belief that you can't start Corum without a Kyren injury. Kyren remains the RB1.
